retrieval_policy.purpose: Provide practical Revit knowledge for AI retrieval without granting Standards authority to examples, candidate values, or unresolved source material.
required_behavior: Always expose knowledge_status and authority_status when returning working-library values.
Never present reference_example or candidate values as approved enterprise defaults.
Preserve unresolved fields rather than inventing values.
Prefer a governed Standards object when it answers the same question.
Project-specific configuration overrides working-library examples when the project authority is established.
A working-library QA finding is evidence only and does not create acceptance authority.
Tool/export presets remain configuration unless separately governed as reusable authority.
Actual source values may be retained when useful, but their source status and promotion readiness must remain explicit.

sanitization.rule: Do not store source-organization, client or project names in working-library record titles, IDs, examples, provenance labels or values. Repository-owned technical identifiers and public classification/product terms may remain where required for meaning.

provenance.migration_note: Working-library records preserve useful source examples and candidate values as non-authoritative AI retrieval data. Source-organization, client and project identifiers are intentionally removed.
